summary.headline: The plugin never renders: the host accepts its projection but the client view is never produced, so neither the session badge nor the per-turn badge appears anywhere.

checks.expected: package installs and the profile lists it
checks.actual: rejected: 'Plugin @steven-wu/dsh-cost-meter@0.1.0-rc.3 is incompatible with dsh 0.2.0-rc.2: peerDependencies {@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime:^0.1.0-rc.6, @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection:^0.1.0-rc.6, @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-conversation:^0.1.0-rc.6}' — nothing installed; succeeded only after `dsh plugin allow-version ... --dsh-version 0.2.0-rc.2 --accept-risk`
checks.note: Install-face fact, not a UI defect. The declared peer range ^0.1.0-rc.6 does not cover the 0.2.0-rc.2 host.

checks.item: Whole-session cost badge appears in the session header on a session that has token usage
checks.actual: 0 badges. Measured across 6 synthetic sessions, 3 viewports, light and dark, after reload, after session switching and after a cold restart: .dsh-cost-badge count is 0 in every sample.

checks.item: Why the badge never renders: projection-registration contract mismatch
checks.expected: the unit registers with the field names the host reads (stateSchema + wire.viewSchema/wire.view)
checks.actual: the plugin passes {key, schema, init, apply, view, stateVersion}; the host's SessionProjectionRegistry.register reads definition.stateSchema and definition.wire. Result: on the host side the stored definition has stateSchema===undefined and wire===undefined, and every client-view path skips the key (`if (def.wire === void 0) continue`).
checks.note: The fold and the persistence both work: the projection cache holds a sessionCost row (ver 3, seq 11, input 1, inputUsd 6.525e-7, priced true). Only the client view is dropped. Host source: dsh-session-projection/lib/index.js lines 69-80 (register) and 247 (`if (def.wire === void 0) continue`).

checks.item: Per-turn cost at the end of each assistant message
checks.expected: each assistant message footer shows that turn's cost
checks.actual: 0 rendered. The conversation.chat.assistant-actions slot exists and has 0 children from this plugin.
checks.note: Blocked by the same A-02 root cause; TurnCostBadge returns null because useProjection('sessionCost') is undefined.

checks.item: Hovering the badge expands a breakdown (input / output / cache-read / cache-write with amounts and token counts)
checks.expected: a tooltip with 4 bucket lines plus the model line
checks.actual: not reachable — there is no badge to hover. No .dsh-cost-tip node exists in any sample.
checks.note: Cannot be observed without a rendered badge. The tooltip implementation itself (fixed-position span, lines joined with newlines, four buckets) was read in the shipped bundle but not exercised.

checks.item: USD symbol and decimal places, including very small amounts
checks.expected: a $ prefix and enough precision that a small amount does not read as zero
checks.actual: formatUsd is $ + toFixed(2) at >=1, toFixed(4) at >=0.01, otherwise toFixed(5). A 1-token turn (0.0000006525 USD) formats as '$0.00000' — indistinguishable from a free turn. Amounts are arithmetically correct; the floor is display precision.
checks.note: Verified by driving the plugin's own unmodified init/apply/view and transcribing its formatUsd from the shipped bundle. Because of A-02 this never reaches the screen; the formatting fact stands on its own.

checks.item: Computed cost agrees with the official price list for the models the host actually offers
checks.expected: host model deepseek-flash priced from its own official rate
checks.actual: The host's catalog offers exactly two models: deepseek-flash (default) and deepseek-v4-pro. The plugin's table keys are deepseek-official/deepseek-v4-pro and deepseek-official/deepseek-v4-flash. deepseek-flash does not match, so priceOf falls back to the default row (the v4-pro rates), and 1M input + 1M output is reported as $2.61 where the official off-peak price is $0.75 — about 3.48x too high.
checks.note: Official source https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing fetched 2026-10-22T01:48Z (UTC clock of this machine). Off-peak = half of peak; peak is 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC Mon-Fri. The v4-pro row is within ~1.1% of the official off-peak figure; the flash row never matches because the host uses the id deepseek-flash (the legacy deepseek-v4-flash alias is retired per the official footnote).
checks.caveat: The composer in evidence/p10-1440-main.png shows 'deepseek-official/deepseek-v4-flash' because that screenshot is of my own fixture session, whose stored model id I set to deepseek-v4-flash; the composer echoes the session's stored model. The host's own catalog (dumped above, evidence/p08-model-catalog.json) offers only deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro, and names deepseek-flash as the default. So a user starting a normal session gets deepseek-flash, which is the id the price table misses.

checks.item: A model id that is not in the price table
checks.expected: either a clear 'unpriced' indication or a documented fallback
checks.actual: silently priced with the default row, with no marker anywhere in the view. some-vendor/mystery-model-9000 yields exactly the same 2.61 as deepseek-v4-pro for the same token counts.

checks.item: Values survive refresh, session switching and a cold restart
checks.actual: the folded state does persist (projection-cache rows exist and survive a restart), but there is nothing displayed to compare, so the user-visible half of this check cannot be settled.
checks.note: Backend persistence is real and verified; the 'does the number stay on screen' question is unanswerable while the badge never renders.

checks.item: Readable at narrow widths and in dark theme; does not cover the composer
checks.expected: no horizontal overflow, no overlap with the input area
checks.actual: no horizontal overflow at 1440 / 1000 / 760 / 600 px and no overlap, but only because nothing is drawn. Dark theme likewise renders nothing from this plugin.
checks.note: Passing this check is not evidence of good layout; there are no elements to lay out.

checks.item: Extreme usage: 1 token, tens of millions of tokens
checks.actual: 1 token -> 6.525e-7 USD, shown as '$0.00000'; 48M/12M/9.6M/2M tokens -> 55.0188 USD, shown as '$55.02'. No overflow, no NaN, no scientific notation, no negative values.

checks.expected: badges stay hidden rather than showing $0.00000
checks.actual: with no usage field at all, priced is false and the projection stays empty; with an all-zero usage object, priced is also false and the single turn carries a zero total. Both are correctly suppressed at the component level and would be hidden even if the wire worked.
checks.note: Empty-state logic reads correctly in the shipped code; the suppression can only be observed once the wire exists.

checks.item: Does the plugin read or send anything it should not
checks.expected: no network, no credentials, no session exfiltration
checks.actual: host half only registers a projection and reads one local JSON price file; client half only reads a projection and renders a span. No fetch/XHR/WebSocket to any host other than 127.0.0.1 in any sample; no credential or token read observed in source or traffic.

reading.writesOutsideDshHome: one, my own probe's fault — see note

checks.note: On first boot with no pricing file the plugin writes ~/.dsh/cost-pricing.json by design. My first registry probe ran without DSH_HOME so it wrote C:\Users\USER\.dsh\cost-pricing.json; I verified the creation timestamp was mine, removed it, kept a copy at evidence/stray-created-by-my-probe-cost-pricing.json, and pinned DSH_COST_PRICING for every later run.

notTested: Hover tooltip content and positioning (no badge to hover)
Any visual property of the badge (size, colour, contrast) at any width or theme
Real billing agreement (no model was called; all amounts are computed from a price table)
Whether the numbers refresh live during a streaming turn (no model call allowed)
